issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who acquires land after public acquisition notice is ordinarily not entitled to benefits under a policy that reserves alternative developed land for the owner whose land was acquired.
material_facts: The acquisition notice was published before the appellant purchased the land.

The policy provided alternative developed land to qualifying owners whose land was acquired, and the relevant category allowed an owner holding more than two but less than twenty acres to seek a portion of the developed land.

The appellant applied for a policy benefit and deposited compensation she had received, but the Trust learned that she had purchased the land after the acquisition notice only when she later produced her title deed.
No order granting the appellant the policy benefit had been passed and no agreement to lease land to her had been entered into.
issues.conclusion: The appellant, as a purchaser after the acquisition notice, was not entitled to the land-policy benefit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1) and 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, publication of the acquisition notice informs the public that the land is needed or likely to be needed for a public purpose and makes subsequent alienations ineffective against the Government or the acquisition beneficiary; on possession, the land vests in the State free of encumbrances. A subsequent purchaser's rights are subject to the Act and may include a right to compensation, but not an alternative site under a policy conferring that benefit on the owner whose land was acquired. The Court relied on Union of India v. Shri Shivkumar Bhargava and distinguished the limited clarification in the Government Order of June 2, 1972.

rule.if: policy_claim_by_transferee and purchase_after_public_acquisition_notice and not (timely_policy_application and benefit_order_passed and lease_agreement_entered)

predicates.policy_claim_by_transferee: The proceeding concerns a transferee's claim for an alternative developed site under a policy associated with compulsory acquisition.
predicates.purchase_after_public_acquisition_notice: The claimant acquired the land after public notice of the proposed acquisition had been published.
predicates.timely_policy_application: The claimant applied within the prescribed time to obtain the policy benefit.
predicates.benefit_order_passed: An order granting the claimant the policy benefit had been passed.
predicates.lease_agreement_entered: An agreement to lease the alternative land to the claimant had been entered into.

issues.definition: When a transferee claims an alternative developed site after acquiring land following public acquisition notice, the transferee is ineligible unless the timely application, benefit-order, and lease-agreement predicates are all present.

issues.legal_issue: A clarification allowing some post-notice purchasers to receive policy benefits applies only when the stated conditions are met and does not generally amend the policy's exclusion of subsequent purchasers.
material_facts: The later Government Order stated that benefits could be given to persons who applied within time, had an order passed in their favour granting the benefit, and had entered into agreements, although they had purchased after publication of the acquisition notice.

The Government Order was issued in response to a specific concern involving three co-owners whose strip of land remained outside an allotment; it was not a general replacement of the existing policy or earlier Government Order.

Although the appellant applied within time, the Trust did not know she was a post-notice purchaser when she applied, no benefit order was passed in her favour, and no lease agreement was entered into.
issues.conclusion: The later Government Order did not assist the appellant because she had not satisfied all of its conditions; it was a limited clarification, not a general extension of the policy to subsequent purchasers.
issues.legal_principle: The June 2, 1972 Government Order must be read with the earlier land policy and Government Order, not as superseding them. Its exception is confined to cases in which the claimant applied within time, an order granting the policy benefit was passed, and an agreement for the lease was entered into. The Court treated the clarification as addressing a limited contingent circumstance rather than establishing a general entitlement for post-notice purchasers.

rule.if: policy_claim_by_post_notice_purchaser and timely_policy_application and benefit_order_passed and lease_agreement_entered

predicates.policy_claim_by_post_notice_purchaser: The proceeding concerns a claim under an acquisition-related land policy by a person who purchased the land after public acquisition notice.
predicates.timely_policy_application: The claimant applied within the prescribed time to obtain the policy benefit.
predicates.benefit_order_passed: An order granting the claimant the policy benefit had been passed.
predicates.lease_agreement_entered: An agreement to lease the alternative land to the claimant had been entered into.

issues.definition: A post-notice purchaser's claim falls within the limited exception when the claimant applied on time, received an order granting the benefit, and entered into a lease agreement.

issues.legal_issue: Equal protection does not entitle a claimant to repeat a benefit given to others in a special case or to perpetuate an erroneous benefit.
material_facts: The appellant argued that denying her the benefit was discriminatory because other persons had received benefits under the Government Orders.
The benefit had been given to three co-owners as a special case because their strip of land remained outside the allotment and was unsuitable or inconvenient to use independently.
The general policy consistently excluded purchasers who acquired land after publication of the acquisition notice.
issues.conclusion: The denial of the benefit was not invidiously discriminatory, and any benefit wrongly given to others did not entitle the appellant to the same benefit.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 of the Constitution does not require the repetition or perpetuation of a wrong. A claimant cannot demand equal treatment with beneficiaries whose benefits arose from a special, materially different circumstance, or obtain a benefit merely because it may have been wrongly granted to others.

predicates.equal_protection_challenge_to_denial: The proceeding includes a challenge that denying a claimed benefit while others received it violated equal protection.
predicates.other_benefit_confined_to_special_circum: The benefit given to others arose from a specific circumstance not shared by the claimant.
predicates.claim_seeks_repetition_of_that_benefit: The claimant seeks the same benefit on the ground that it was granted to others, including where that grant may have been erroneous.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges a denial by relying on a benefit granted to others in special circumstances, equal protection does not provide an entitlement to repeat that benefit.
